## Active

::: {#list-active}
:::

<p style="font-size: 0.95em; color: var(--bs-secondary-color); margin-bottom: -1.5em; max-width: 900px;">

  `multiRL` is not simply a larger version or straightforward extension of `binaryRL` (much like how an F-test is not just a “bigger” t-test). The difference is not merely about displaying more bandits on the screen. Instead, `multiRL` supports more complex cognitive architectures, including latent rule learning, simultaneous updating of multiple Q-tables (e.g., RL + WM systems), and a much more flexible platform for model construction. It also supports a wider range of parameter estimation approaches, including MLE, MAP, ABC, and RNN-based methods.

  Although the two packages differ substantially in functionality, they share a very similar high-level structure. This allows users who are already familiar with `binaryRL` to transition smoothly to `multiRL` with minimal additional learning. At the same time, `multiRL` introduces many new interfaces and customization options, giving advanced users much greater flexibility in defining complex models.

</p>
